speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin assessing your postpartum fever and abdominal tenderness, could you please tell me how many days or weeks have passed since your delivery? Additionally, have you noticed any unusual discharge from the vagina, such as foul odor or heavy bleeding?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. On a scale of 0 to 10, how would you rate the severity of your abdominal pain, and have you noticed any redness, warmth, or swelling at the site of any episiotomy or lacerations? Also, are you currently able to pass urine without significant difficulty or pain?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Uterine tenderness. I also have Decreased bowel sounds, Increased frequency of urination, Fever.

speaker: Doctor
text: You have uterine tenderness, decreased bowel sounds, urinary frequency, and fever, which raises concern for endometritis or a urinary tract infection. To help differentiate, do you have any pain or burning sensation when you urinate, and have you noticed any foul-smelling vaginal discharge? I will also request a Complete Blood Count and a Urinalysis to check for signs of infection.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Uncomplicated pregnancy leading up to a vaginal delivery. No significant past medical or surgical history. Social history: Does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. Lives with her partner.
